items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 17 at 7:38PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
Heavy rain and strong winds are expected to start Friday and last
through the weekend as multiple strong low pressure systems move
into the northern gulf. These lows will bring multiple days of
moderate to heavy rain, with around 1.5 to 3 inches of rain every 24
hours. Some areas, especially near Yakutat and along the gulf coast,
could see localized areas reach around 4 inches of rain in 24 hours.
Heaviest rain rates are anticipated late Saturday into Sunday with
hourly rates of 0.15 to 0.3 inch

items.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 17 at 10:47AM AKDT until September 19 at 8:45AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Chena River Basin from Moose Creek Dam to the end of Chena
Hot Springs Road.

* WHEN...Until 845 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. River or stream flows are elevated. Ponding of
water in areas is occurring or is imminent.

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 16 at 2:12PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Upper Kuskokwim Valley

Recent heavy rains have fallen across Western Alaska. Water levels
along streams and rivers will continue to slowly recede through
Wednesday night then slowly rise again Thursday morning as the
rainfall from the recent Bering storm moves downstream. Water levels
this weekend are not expected to be as high in comparison to last
week.

For more updated river information, please refer to water.noaa.gov or
weather.gov/aprfc.
